t:
(a) 
None of the funds appropriated by this or any other Act may be expended by any Federal Agency to procure any product or service that is subject to the provisions of Public Law 89–306 and that will be available under the procurement by the Administrator of General Services known as “FTS2000” unless—

        (1) 
such product or service is procured by the Administrator of General Services as part of the procurement known as “FTS2000”; or
 
        (2) 
that agency establishes to the satisfaction of the Administrator of General Services that—

            (A) 
that agency’s requirements for such procurement are unique and cannot be satisfied by property and service procured by the Administrator of General Services as part of the procurement known as “FTS2000”; and
 
            (B) 
the agency procurement, pursuant to such delegation, would be cost-effective and would not adversely affect the cost-effectiveness of the FTS2000 procurement.
   
    (b) 
After July 31, 1996, subsection (a) shall apply only if the Administrator of General Services has reported that the FTS2000 procurement is producing prices that allow the Government to satisfy its requirements for such procurement in the most cost-effective manner.
 
    (c) 
The Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct and deliver a comprehensive analysis of the cost to the Federal Government of all Federal agency telecommunications services and traffic, by agency, and provide such report to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations by no later than May 31, 1996: Provided, That such report shall (1) identify which agencies are using FTS2000 systems; (2) determine whether or not such usage is cost-effective; and (3) provide a comparison of telecommunication costs between agencies that use or do not use FTS2000.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the agency showing made "to the satisfaction of the Administrator of General Services" and the Comptroller General's report are consultative procedures. Every actor involved is inside the federal government: federal agencies, the GSA Administrator, the Comptroller General, and congressional appropriations committees. Intra-government coordination and reports to Congress are not participation, and no outside party, comment period, rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue appears in the section.
fable.s: provide such report to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations by no later than May 31, 1996

opus.w: The only interactions are between federal agencies and the GSA Administrator, and a Comptroller General report to congressional committees. All of these actors are inside the federal government. No state, company, expert or member of the public is consulted or given a role, so this is coordination and reporting within the government, not participation.
opus.s: that agency establishes to the satisfaction of the Administrator of General Services that—
opus.b:
**Step 1.** The tempting reading is that agencies must "establish to the satisfaction of the Administrator" before procuring, and that the Comptroller General must deliver a report. Both look like formal processes. But every actor here is inside the federal government: the procuring Federal agencies, the Administrator of General Services, the Comptroller General, and the House and Senate Appropriations Committees. Nobody outside the government is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue. FTS2000 is just the name of a procurement.

**Step 2.**

qwen_chat.w: The section describes a process where one federal agency (the procuring agency) must justify its actions to another federal official (the Administrator of General Services). Both parties are inside the federal government. There is no requirement for consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities. The report to Congress is also an internal government action.
qwen_chat.s: that agency establishes to the satisfaction of the Administrator of General Services that— (A) that agency’s requirements for such procurement are unique and cannot be satisfied by property and service procured by the Administrator of General Services as part of the procurement known as “FTS2000”; and (B) the agency procurement, pursuant to such delegation, would be cost-effective and would not adversely affect the cost-effectiveness of the FTS2000 procurement.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for an agency to "establish to the satisfaction of the Administrator of General Services" that its requirements are unique constitutes a form of consultation or coordination with an outside party. However, the Administrator of General Services is a federal official, and the agency seeking the exemption is also a federal agency. This is intra-governmental coordination and oversight, not participation by non-federal entities. The report to Congress is also internal to the government.
